question: Does the `scripts` stage of verify.ps1 redden, cleanly attributed to scripts/test-run-game-capture-parameters.ps1, when scripts/run-game.ps1's screenshot precondition regresses to requiring only two of the three pixel-affecting parameters (drops the -UiScale guard) - the same class of defect as the first mutant, applied to the second, independent fix in this Issue?
preconditions: Run only after committing the fixed, checked-in state (commit a3ff6e5) - `git status --short` was clean before the mutation was applied.

mutant.failingAssertion: 'run-game.ps1' no longer requires -UiScale for a screenshot capture: no guard appends it to $missingCaptureParameters when $hasUiScale is false

gitStateBeforeAndAfter: git status --short clean before mutating (commit a3ff6e5 already made); git checkout -- scripts/run-game.ps1 restored the fix afterward, then git status --short clean again.
conclusion: The `scripts` stage reddens (exit 1, verification_result status=error, failedStage=scripts) when run-game.ps1's screenshot-capture precondition regresses to checking only two of the three required parameters, and the failure is attributed by scripts/test-run-game-capture-parameters.ps1 by exact missing parameter name rather than surfacing as a generic test failure or, worse, silently letting the request reach a full build and the engine's own ArgumentException. The mutation was reverted immediately after this run; it was never committed. Combined with evidence/329-mutant.json (the resolver-contract mutant on the first, independent fix in this Issue), both defects this Issue closed now have a check that reddens on regression, not just a one-time manual proof.
